To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
diffusible gradients of factors derived from denervated peripheral nerves direct the regeneration of motor axons in vitro and in vivo.
concentration gradients of target derived factors direct the outgrowth both during development and regeneration, in vivo as well as in vitro.
diffusible gradients of target-derived Schwann cell-released factors direct axon growth both during development and regeneration, in vivo as well as in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of target-derived factors in the guidance of developing and regenerating axons in vivo and in the guidance of growth cones of developing and regenerative neurons in vitro.
the molecular and cellular basis of axon guidance.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that guide regenerating axons in the peripheral nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diffusible chemoattractive factors are involved in the regeneration of adult peripheral nerves.
during regeneration, motor neurons respond to concentration gradients in vivo and in vivo, as well as sensory neurons do in vitro.
diffusible factors released by Schwann cells and other cell types from denervated peripheral nerves direct the regeneration of motor and sensory axons in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the peripheral nerve is an excellent model for studying regeneration and the mechanisms that direct axon growth.

the same target-derived diffusible factors that guide the developing axons in vivo also guide the regeneration of adult axons in vivo and that the mechanism of guidance in vivo is the same as the guidance in vitro.

The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that diffusing factors from denervated peripheral nerves can be used to guide regenerating adult motor neuron axons in vivo.
the same molecules that direct the outgrowth and regeneration of axons during development also direct regeneration in the adult.
